sweep5.detail: Walked the spec's 21 sections in order and proved each named artefact with a command. Roles & Permission Matrix -> 6 capabilities: `create-request`/`view-own-requests`/`view-all-requests` in CAPABILITY_MATRIX (index.ts:582-584, grants at :620-622, :650-652, :680-682, :710-712) and `CreateRequest`/`ViewOwnRequests`/`ViewAllRequests` in roles.ts:82-84 with grants at :114-116, :139-141, :147, :150 — matching the matrix row for row, viewer holding view-own-requests only. Functional requirements 1-47 -> parsers in packages/validation/src/requests.ts and services under apps/api/src/requests. API Contracts -> 8 route headings, 11 handlers in requests.controller.ts:39-165, all under `@UseGuards(SessionGuard, OrgScopeGuard)` at :34-35; the reassign contract's stated capability matches `@RequireCapability('ViewAllRequests')` at :168. Data Model -> 3 tables compared field-by-field against migration.sql: Request 21/21, RequestMessage 6/6, RequestEvent 11/11, no column in one and not the other; 6 indexes (the unique `(organizationId, number)` plus the three the spec names, plus one each on the child tables) present verbatim at migration.sql:71-80; 9 FKs with the stated onDelete. The one change to an existing table is `ALTER TABLE "Organization" ADD COLUMN "nextRequestNumber" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` (migration.sql:11) — additive with a default, so the previous image keeps working against the new schema (CLAUDE.md migration rule). New Enums -> a deliberate 'none', and none were added. Error Messages -> 31 rows compared by script against REQUEST_MESSAGES (index.ts:1771-1840): 0 missing, 0 mismatched (one apparent mismatch on `editForbidden` was my scanner hitting MEMBER_MESSAGES at :493 first; the requests key at :1828 is byte-identical). Required data-testid -> 46 ids, all present under apps/web; the four template-literal ones confirmed by hand at RequestRow.tsx:66, :94, :120, :129. Test Cases -> 41 ids (6 UNIT, 22 INT, 13 E2E), all referenced from apps/api/test, packages/validation/src or e2e/tests, 0 unreferenced; the 11 TC-01 ids in code that are not in this spec belong to clients and signup, not to this area. Acceptance Criteria -> 17 rows, every one carrying an observer in the Observing-each-criterion table at :864-878, and every TC it names exists. Requirement 47's negative artefact confirmed: no mail import anywhere under apps/api/src/requests. Every section contributed at least one artefact except Out of Scope and Known Gaps, which state non-goals, and DS gaps, which names two absences rather than artefacts.

blastRadius.detail: Traced outward from the three shared things this change touches. (1) packages/validation/src/roles.ts gives ROLE_CAPABILITIES.user and .viewer their first non-empty grants, so capabilitiesFor on those roles now returns a capability where it returned none. No @RequireCapability gate reads CreateRequest or ViewOwnRequests, and the only decorator added is ViewAllRequests at requests.controller.ts:168, whose grants for user and viewer are unchanged — so no existing endpoint changes its answer. (2) The sidebar nav array: the Requests entry moved from `can(role,'view-requests')` to unconditional, which is what requirement 38 asks for and what CLAUDE.md's no-dead-links rule now permits because every role can use the destination. No other entry moved. (3) The badge hook's field rename pendingCount -> badgeCount: `grep -rn usePendingRequests apps/web` gives four call sites, and the three that are not Sidebar.tsx destructure `refresh` alone, so the rename reaches exactly one reader. `totalCount` is gone from apps/web entirely and the only caller of GET .../requests outside the requests pages is the badge provider. On the API side, RequestsService, RequestEventsService and VacationRequestFeedService are imported by app.module.ts and by nothing else, so the extraction of the vacation feed is contained. Outside the product: scripts/wf.mjs and scripts/ship.mjs change the pipeline for every future run of every spec, and CLAUDE.md's deploy note puts scripts/ among the paths copied into no image, so the blast radius there is reviews and runs rather than the deployed system.

findings.claim: `if (replans) run.specSha = sha` records a fact about the future. The guard at :569 exists to enforce "handoff.json was compiled from the spec on disk" — that is what its own failure message says. After :610 the question the code asks is "does the spec on disk equal the sha recorded at init, or at the last resume that merely asked for a replan", and those stop being the same question the moment the replan is requested and does not happen. The fix for pass 2's F2 turned a false refusal into a false acceptance: the same guard now waves through the exact state it exists to catch, and the command prints "handoff.json still describes this spec" while doing so.

witness.detail: A run halts at review with a spec-defect finding. The person corrects specs/requests/01-requests.md from sha S0 to S1, commits, and runs `node scripts/wf.mjs resume --stage pre_implement --accept-spec-edits`. wf.mjs:565 sets replans=true, :610 sets run.specSha=S1, the reset loop at :629-632 marks pre_implement..qa pending, run.status='pre_implement'. handoff.json on disk is still the S0 plan. ship.mjs starts the pre-implementer and the orchestrator is killed before handoff.json is rewritten — the abandoned-run state the entry guard at :562 was widened to admit. The person then runs `node scripts/wf.mjs resume --stage implement`. :562 passes (status is not 'ready'), :569 passes because sha(S1) === run.specSha(S1), :583 passes because no spec file has changed since the last resume, and :641 prints "spec sha matches the one recorded at init — handoff.json still describes this spec". ship.mjs:414 then takes `stage = run.status` and ship.mjs:147 tells the implementer to implement `.workflow/runs/<id>/handoff.json` — the S0 plan, compiled from the spec review found defective — and review and QA are measured against it. Before this commit step 4 was refused, because run.specSha still held S0. Nothing else re-checks it: cmdResume never verifies that the stages before the resume target passed, and no code path between the resume and the implementer prompt reads handoff.json's provenance.
witness.source: .claude/skills/code-review/SKILL.md:118 — "**Blocks when those are not the same question.**", under "10. Predicate sweep": "write two things — the rule it is there to enforce, and the exact question the code asks"

findings.suggestedFix: Stamp the sha where the plan is actually rebuilt rather than where the rebuild is requested: record the intent at resume (`run.pendingSpecSha = sha`) and promote it to `run.specSha` when pre_implement records a passing verdict, so `specSha` keeps meaning "the sha handoff.json was compiled from" and the guard at :569 keeps asking that question. If the assignment must stay in cmdResume, the resume-past-pre_implement path needs its own predicate — `run.stages.pre_implement.status === 'passed'` at a time later than the last resumes entry — because the sha alone can no longer tell the two states apart.

findings.claim: `run.findingHistory` is only ever incremented and is initialised empty at cmdInit; nothing clears an entry when the finding under that key is confirmed closed. The key is `rule@file#symbol`, so a genuinely new defect at a site that has already had two different ones fixed inherits their count and is declared "stuck — the requirement is ambiguous or the finding is wrong" on its first appearance. That is this verdict's own situation: `.claude/skills/code-review/SKILL.md#10 Predicate sweep@scripts/wf.mjs#cmdResume` stands at 2 for two findings I have just confirmed closed, and F1 is a third and different defect. The 4e158cc commit fixed the neighbouring version of this — two findings in one verdict sharing a key — by deduplicating within the verdict, which leaves the across-verdicts case untouched.

witness.detail: run.json findingHistory holds `".claude/skills/code-review/SKILL.md#10 Predicate sweep@scripts/wf.mjs#cmdResume": 2`, and priorBlockers above record both of those findings as closed against their witnesses. With cfg.convergence.autoContestAfter = 2 (.claude/ai-workflow.config.json), route() at :281 will read 3 for F1 and halt with 'stuck-finding' rather than routing it to the implementer — a correct outcome here, since a person should decide whether this resume design is worth another cycle, but reached by counting two fixed defects as attempts at a third.

findings.suggestedFix: Clear a key when a later verdict's priorBlockers report it closed, or key the counter on the finding's witness rather than on `rule@file#symbol`, so "the same finding twice" means the same defect twice.

findings.claim: The loop that closes a killed stage covers `STAGES.slice(0, STAGES.indexOf(stage))` only, so the commonest abandoned-run case — the stage that was killed is the one being resumed — emits no `stage-end` event. The reset loop that follows sets it to `pending`, which fixes `wf status`, but the board reads the attempt's artefacts and not run.json: run-report.mjs:177-179 marks any attempt with a `startedAt` and no `.log` and no end event as `running` with `endedAt = Date.now()`, so the killed attempt keeps counting upward for as long as the record exists — the exact thing the comment at :618-621 says this loop exists to prevent.

witness.detail: The orchestrator dies mid-implement and `wf resume --stage implement` is run. STAGES.slice(0, 2) covers preflight and pre_implement, so implement gets no stage-end event; run-report.mjs:167 finds a startedAt, :172 finds no `.log`, :177-179 sets state='running' and endedAt=Date.now(). `npm run board` shows that attempt still growing.

findings.suggestedFix: Close a `running` stage at the resume point as well as before it — it is over either way, and the resume is the moment a person confirms that.
